Project 02 · Subscription ecosystem

Turning a loyalty program into an everyday subscription.

I helped shape Smiles+ from an early business proposition into an end-to-end subscription product, connecting the existing Clube Smiles ecosystem with entertainment partners across acquisition, billing, activation and ongoing management.

RoleSenior Product Designer
ScopeProduct strategy, IA, interaction, UI, prototyping, design system
PlatformWeb & mobile
DomainLoyalty, subscription, entertainment

Clube Smiles
CLUBE SMILES+

Travel benefits meet everyday entertainment.

One subscription combining miles, Smiles benefits and a streaming service customers can change every month.

Portfolio reconstruction. The interface uses the product rules, visual language and content patterns from the original project and current Smiles+ experience.

Section

Context

Smiles already had a subscription. The opportunity was to make it mean more.

Clube Smiles created a recurring relationship through miles and travel benefits. Smiles+ extended that relationship with entertainment services customers could use between trips, without replacing the product they already knew.

Existing ecosystem

Clube Smiles

Miles, travel benefits, recurring billing and an established customer relationship.

New layer

Everyday value

Entertainment benefits create utility outside the moment of planning or taking a trip.

0→1 challenge

One product

Turn partners, billing and activation dependencies into one coherent subscription.

The model was familiar. The ecosystem wasn't.

Section

Product definition

A simple proposition quickly became a system of product questions.

Clube Smiles + entertainment→Eligibility→Choice→Billing→Activation→Management

Who is eligible? What exactly is included? Which payment relationship applies? When is the benefit actually usable? How can it change? What happens if the base subscription is suspended or cancelled?

Market reference

Meli+ helped frame the model

A known ecosystem-subscription pattern helped Business discuss the opportunity. The design problem was translating the logic into Smiles, not copying another interface.

Design question

Keep complexity behind the interface

How might we translate an ecosystem subscription model into Smiles without making customers understand the organizational complexity behind it?

Section

Lifecycle

We stopped thinking about checkout and started thinking about the subscription lifecycle.

Discover→Choose→Subscribe→Pay→Activate→Use→Manage→Change

Designing the whole life of a subscription, not just the sale.

Section

Final experience

The visual system had to make four very different services feel like one product decision.

Section

Measurement framework

Conversion tells us whether customers bought the proposition. Activation tells us whether the product delivered it.

Targets, not reported results. The project was still evolving when I left; these KPIs frame how I would instrument and evaluate the new product after launch.

Reflection

The interface was the simplest layer of a much larger system.

Smiles+ reinforced something central to how I approach Product Design: the work is often translating business rules, an existing ecosystem, billing, external partners and customer expectations into one understandable product. Designing the whole lifecycle made the difference between creating a purchase flow and creating a subscription experience.

A good subscription isn't finished when someone buys it.
